Simulate Waterfall Drug-Combination Trials

Source: R/waterfall_simulate.R
waterfall_simulate.Rd

Simulate trials of two drugs given together, run with the waterfall design of Zhang and Yuan (2016), which looks for the MTD contour, that is, for one MTD at every dose level of drug A. This is the simulation engine behind sim_waterfall, exposed for users who want the raw trial data.

Usage

waterfall_simulate(
  target,
  p_true,
  cohort_size,
  n_cohort = NULL,
  n_trials = 10000,
  n_earlystop = 12,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  extrasafe = FALSE,
  offset = 0.05,
  titration = FALSE,
  bound_mtd = FALSE,
  boin_compatible = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, for example 0.30.

p_true

Numeric matrix. True DLT probability of each dose combination, with one row per dose level of drug A and one column per dose level of drug B, both in increasing dose order. It needs at least two rows and no more rows than columns.

cohort_size

Integer scalar. Number of patients per cohort.

n_cohort

Integer vector with one element per dose level of drug A, or NULL. Maximum number of cohorts of the first, second, ... subtrial. Defaults to NULL, which gives every subtrial about four patients per dose of the subtrial (see Details).

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar. A subtrial ends once this many patients have been treated at the dose chosen for its next cohort. Defaults to 12.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. Posterior probability cutoff for eliminating a combination. Defaults to 0.95.

extrasafe

Logical scalar. Apply the stricter safety stopping rule at the lowest dose of every subtrial. Defaults to FALSE.

offset

Numeric scalar between 0 and 0.5. Amount by which cutoff_eli is relaxed for the safety stopping rule. Defaults to 0.05.

titration

Logical scalar. Start the first subtrial with one patient per dose, up to the first DLT. Ignored when cohort_size is one. Defaults to FALSE.

bound_mtd

Logical scalar. Require the estimate at the candidate MTD of a subtrial to be below the de-escalation boundary. Defaults to FALSE.

boin_compatible

Logical scalar. Drop the data of a subtrial that ends without a candidate MTD, as BOIN::get.oc.comb() does (see Details). Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class waterfall_trials, which is a list with components

n_pts

Integer array with dimensions trial by level of drug A by level of drug B: number of patients treated at each combination.

n_tox

Integer array of the same dimensions: number of DLTs observed.

eliminated

Logical array of the same dimensions: whether the combination is excluded from the selection of the MTD contour.

n_subtrials

Integer vector: number of subtrials run in each trial.

n_enrolled

Integer vector: number of patients treated in each trial, including those of a subtrial whose data were dropped.

stop_reason

Character vector: why each trial ended.

boundary

The boin_boundary object used for the decisions.

settings

List of the design parameters.

Details

The dose matrix is divided into one-dimensional subtrials, each run with the BOIN design for a single agent. The first subtrial starts at the lowest combination, moves up the first column (the lowest level of drug B) to the highest level of drug A and then along that row. When a subtrial ends, the dose whose isotonic estimate of the DLT probability is closest to target is its candidate MTD. The next subtrial runs along the row below the row of the candidate, over the second to the last level of drug B, and starts one level of drug B above the candidate (at the last level when the candidate is there). The trial ends after the subtrial of the lowest level of drug A.

Within a subtrial, the dose escalates, stays or de-escalates by the boundaries of boin_boundary; a dose with too many DLTs is eliminated together with the doses above it, and the subtrial ends without a candidate when its lowest dose is eliminated. Otherwise a subtrial ends when n_earlystop patients have been treated at the dose chosen for the next cohort, or when its maximum number of cohorts, n_cohort, is reached. The default of n_cohort is ceiling(round(4 / cohort_size, 2) * m) for a subtrial of m doses, the default of the reference implementation, which follows the article's suggestion of four patients per dose.

The rules are those of BOIN::get.oc.comb() with mtd.contour = TRUE in version 2.7.2 of the 'BOIN' package, the implementation by the authors of the article. Random variates are drawn one per patient in enrollment order, as that function draws them, so with boin_compatible = TRUE, the same seed and matching arguments the two give the same trials. Three rules of that function are not in the article:

  • When the candidate MTD of the first subtrial lies in the first column below the highest level of drug A, the rows above it are excluded, and when the data at the candidate would lead to an escalation, an additional subtrial explores the rest of its row.

  • The combinations to the right of a candidate MTD in its row are excluded from the selection of the MTD contour.

  • The trial ends when a subtrial ends without a candidate MTD; the rows below are then not explored.

With extrasafe = TRUE, that function evaluates the safety rule with a Beta(y + 0.05, n - y + 0.1) distribution during a subtrial and with a Beta(y + 1, n - y + 1) distribution when it chooses the candidate; the package does the same.

The package differs from that function in two points. When a subtrial other than the additional one ends without a candidate, that function drops its data, so that its patients and DLTs are missing from the counts and a trial stopped in the first subtrial has no patients. By default the package keeps these data and marks every dose of that subtrial as eliminated; boin_compatible = TRUE drops them. And that function takes the escalation and de-escalation boundaries from the default values of p_saf and p_tox whatever values are given; the package uses the values given.

Values of stop_reason are "completed", "first_subtrial_no_mtd", "later_subtrial_no_mtd" and "max_sample_size".

References

Zhang, L. and Yuan, Y. (2016). A Practical Bayesian Design to Identify the Maximum Tolerated Dose Contour for Drug Combination Trials. Statistics in Medicine, 35(27), 4924-4936.

Yan, F., Zhang, L., Zhou, Y., Pan, H., Liu, S. and Yuan, Y. (2020). BOIN: An R Package for Designing Single-Agent and Drug-Combination Dose-Finding Trials Using Bayesian Optimal Interval Designs. Journal of Statistical Software, 94(13), 1-32.

See also

sim_waterfall, waterfall_select_mtd

Examples

p_true <- matrix(c(0.03, 0.10, 0.28,
                   0.10, 0.30, 0.50), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)

trials <- waterfall_simulate(
  target = 0.30,
  p_true = p_true,
  cohort_size = 3,
  n_trials = 200,
  seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated waterfall drug-combination trials
#>   trials          : 200
#>   dose levels     : 2 of drug A, 3 of drug B
#>   target DLT rate : 0.3
#>   cohorts         : at most 6/3 per subtrial, of size 3
#>   max sample size : 27
#> 
#> Average patients treated per trial:
#>      B1   B2   B3
#> A1 3.35 2.01 6.99
#> A2 5.61 6.62 2.37
#> 
#> Average DLTs observed per trial:
#>      B1   B2   B3
#> A1 0.09 0.17 1.97
#> A2 0.50 2.08 1.20
#> 
#> Reason for ending (%):
#> 
#> completed 
#>       100
